name: Jim Desmond
evidence: San Diego County supervisor who made border/illegal immigration a signature theme (called San Diego sector the 'new epicenter' of illegal immigration, attacked the county's sanctuary/anti-ICE-cooperation policy as 'radical'); Trump-endorsed, also Issa-endorsed. No Ukraine record found; one voter guide oddly lists an ICE-tactics resolution, so evidence is mixed.

name: Dan Barrios
evidence: Richardson city councilman running on families, small business, healthcare costs and redistricting reform; rated a moderate Democrat, no progressive-group endorsements or left-economic platform found.

name: Ralph Alvarado
evidence: Launched as a self-described America First movement leader pledging to 'stop the invasion at the southern border' and fight the 'woke agenda' (former Bevin running mate); in Aug 2026 rebranded as an independent-minded, bipartisan healthcare candidate and scrubbed Trump/America First references.

name: Michael Bouchard Jr.
evidence: Army captain/Bronze Star veteran and son of the Oakland County sheriff; platform on border security, energy, hospital price transparency, and criticism of the trade fight with Canada; Trump-endorsed but no nationalist policy signals found.

name: Jennifer Balkcom
evidence: State representative (former Democrat until 2016, mortgage officer) picked by the NC-11 GOP executive committee to replace Chuck Edwards after his withdrawal; conventional conservative state record (citizens-only voting amendment, farmland protection), no Freedom Caucus or America First signals.

name: Jenny Costa Honeycutt
evidence: Charleston County councilwoman and construction attorney who called herself non-polarizing and beat the harder-right state Rep. Mark Smith in the runoff (he attacked her county tax vote); supports a balanced-budget amendment and 287(g); Trump endorsed her as 'America First' only after the runoff.

name: Justin J. Pearson
evidence: Tennessee Three state rep backed by Justice Democrats and Leaders We Deserve, running on Medicare for All and living wages; ousted pro-Israel Rep. Steve Cohen and opposed sending 'billions in bombs' overseas.

name: Jay Feely
evidence: Ex-NFL kicker, Trump-aligned (backs the Iran war, Trump enforcement) but favors streamlined/easier legal immigration and calls for ending tariffs; business-conservative tax/regulation platform, no Ukraine stance found.

name: David Flippo
evidence: Retired Air Force Lt. Col., Trump-endorsed, campaigned on mining, water rights, fuel prices and affordability while pledging to back Trump's agenda; no distinct nationalist policy themes found (campaign dogged by military-record and carpetbagging issues).

name: Aaron Flint
evidence: Conservative talk-radio host and former Zinke state director/Gianforte campaign aide, backed by Trump, Speaker Johnson, Gianforte and the NRCC; platform on housing regulation, trades and timber; raises talk-radio themes (Epstein, trans athletes, immigration) but no Ukraine or Freedom Caucus signals.

name: Joe Mitchell
evidence: Former state rep who worked in the Trump administration; calls the GOP's future 'an America First party', runs an anti-establishment anti-corruption platform (term limits, stock-trading ban, no corporate PAC money) and opposes 'endless wars'.

name: Brinker Harding
evidence: Omaha city council VP and businessman running to succeed Don Bacon on Omaha's balanced-budget/low-crime record, endorsed by Sen. Deb Fischer (and later Trump); framed the race as 'normal vs. crazy'.
